ops.title: HANDOFF: multi-tenant fusekit-holder daemon (durable holder fork-bomb fix)
ops.body:
# HANDOFF — multi-tenant `fusekit-holder` daemon (the durable fork-bomb fix)

**Why:** the 2026-06-24 fork-bomb (cc-notes incident `ef281ea`) came from `proc.Spawn` copying
`os.Executable()` and exec'ing it **per consumer, per mount**, trusting the binary's `main` to route
argv to a holder — false for a test binary (Go's flag parser stops at the non-flag subcommand,
`testing.Main` re-runs the suite, which re-enters the spawn → exponential fork bomb). The immediate
safety net shipped in fusekit **v0.14.2** (RLIMIT_NPROC cap on the spawned child + the `scripts/test.sh`
ulimit harness) bounds any runaway. **This handoff is the DURABLE fix: remove the self-`exec` entirely.**

**Target architecture:** ONE live, system-wide `fusekit-holder` daemon that holds ALL fuse-t mounts for
ALL fusekit consumers (cc-pool, cc-squash, cc-notes). Clients connect to its well-known socket and
`AddMount`/`RemoveMount` over RPC; the daemon mounts/unmounts and supervises. **Not instance-per-mount —
one process, many mounts.** The current per-consumer holder + `Supervisor` lifecycle folds INTO it.

## Components
1. **`fusekit cmd/holder` (`fusekit-holder`)** — a dedicated binary whose `main` ONLY serves (no test
   code, no argv ambiguity). Multi-tenant: a global socket (e.g.
   `~/Library/Application Support/fusekit/holder.sock`), per-client mount ownership, teardown on client
   disconnect, auto-start (LaunchAgent). `proc.Spawn` gains an explicit **`ExecPath`** (set ⇒ exec that
   binary, NOT `os.Executable()`); the `os.Executable()` default stays for consumers that don't opt in.
   Because the holder is a real dedicated binary (never a test binary), the fork-bomb mechanism cannot
   exist.
2. **Own Developer-ID-signed + notarized Homebrew cask** at a stable path. Every fusekit consumer
   declares it as a **cask dependency**. One signed binary at one stable path ⇒ **one "Network Volumes"
   TCC grant, granted once, shared by every mount and client** — replaces the `StableExecDir` copy dance.
3. **Content via the `ContentSource` seam — the SAME one File Provider uses**
   (`fileproviderd.ContentSource`: Manifest/ReadSynth/WriteThrough/Classify). The daemon can't compile in
   any client's FS, so each `AddMount` registers the client's ContentSource callback socket: the daemon
   makes the bulk **live symlinks** itself and PULLS the ~2 synthetic files (`.claude.json`,
   `settings.json`) over RPC. One content seam, both backends (fuse holder + FP). Per-op cost stays low
   (bulk = symlinks; only synthetic files proxied), matching today's perf.
4. **Versioned, multi-client protocol** (the `mountd` discipline extended: frozen + additive-only) — one
   daemon serves clients of *different* fusekit versions; it upgrades on its own cask cadence; clients
   tolerate a newer/older daemon within the compat range.

## Scope / risk (multi-phase; all test runs under `scripts/test.sh` in isolation)
- The daemon itself: multi-tenant service + auto-start + global socket + per-client mount ownership /
  teardown-on-disconnect.
- The content-proxy protocol (reuse `fileproviderd.ContentSource`).
- **Refactor cc-pool's in-process mirror (`InProcessFuse()` / `mountd.Host`) to register over RPC** —
  this touches **DEPLOYED LIVE FUSE** (6 accounts on the user's main machine). Stage + validate under
  `scripts/test.sh` in an isolated env; NEVER exercise the holder spawn on the user's machine outside the
  harness.
- New `fusekit-holder` cask + consumer dependencies; cross-client version skew (the Supervisor's
  skew machinery already anticipates a separately-versioned on-disk binary).
- Shares the `ContentSource` seam and the signed cask with the File-Provider feature — sequence them
  together where the cask/signing overlaps.
- Does NOT block anything; the immediate safety net (v0.14.2) already holds.

## Suggested phasing
1. `cmd/holder` single-tenant + `proc.ExecPath` + the signed cask; migrate cc-pool to spawn it
   (still one holder per cc-pool, content still in-process) — proves the dedicated-binary + cask + TCC
   path end to end.
2. Multi-tenant: `AddMount`/`RemoveMount`, multi-client ownership, one process holding many mounts.
3. ContentSource-over-RPC: migrate cc-pool's mirror off `InProcessFuse()` so content is pulled by the
   daemon over the socket.
4. Onboard cc-squash / cc-notes as additional clients; retire per-consumer holders + `StableExecDir`.

See: cc-notes incident `ef281ea`; memories `fusekit-global-holder-direction`,
`fusekit-holder-fork-bomb-incident`, `cc-pool-fileprovider-signing-reality`,
`fusekit-overlay-ownership-refactor`.
ops.when: building the global fusekit-holder daemon, or replacing the per-consumer self-exec mount-holder with one signed multi-tenant holder (AddMount/RemoveMount RPC, ContentSource); the durable fix for the 2026-06-24 fork-bomb beyond the v0.14.2 safety net
